name: Wallis and Futuna
summary: A red field with a French tricolour, edged in white, in the canton and a white cross pattée formed of four triangles in the centre. The flag is unofficial; officially the territory uses the French tricolour.
origin: The red flag with the white saltire-like cross comes from the flag of the Kingdom of Uvea (Wallis), traditionally associated with the Lavelua, the king of Uvea. The French tricolour was added to the canton.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: From the traditional flag of Uvea.

symbols.name: White cross
symbols.description: Four white triangles meeting at a point, forming a cross pattée.
symbols.meaning: Christianity; from the flag of the Kingdom of Uvea.

facts: Wallis and Futuna still has three traditional kingdoms recognised by France: Uvea, Sigave and Alo.
It is the only French territory whose flag includes the tricolour in a canton.
It lies between Fiji and Samoa.
clues: Red with a French tricolour in the canton and a white cross of four triangles.
Its territory contains three traditional kingdoms.
Its cross came from the flag of a Polynesian kingdom.
